subject: Reserve throughput slot — FinLedger dedicated capacity kickoff

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Quick recap + three times to lock a throughput-sizing slot

Hi Tom / Anjali —

Thanks for the demo/discovery earlier — great conversation and helpful context on your AR reconciliation and fraud-detection flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock a dedicated-capacity sizing call: 

Recap (high level)
- Primary workload: batch + near-real-time scoring for ACH reconciliation and suspicious-activity triage.
- Peak expected QPS: ~6–12 inference requests per second during morning batch, concurrency spikes to ~20 for bursts.
- Typical request size: 300–600 tokens (prompt+context).
- Target P95 latency: <= 250ms for production path; <150ms for interactive ops UI ideal.

What we need for the sizing call
- A 60-minute dedicated session with your infra/ops person + one of our SEs to review throughput, latency targets, and network topology.
- If you can fill the attached pre-call template with actual payload sizes and concurrency profiles that will speed the call. I attached a lightweight spreadsheet: pre-call-throughput-template.xlsx.

Proposed times (all PT) — pick one or propose alternatives:
- Tue, Feb 24 — 10:00am–11:00am PT
- Wed, Feb 25 — 2:00pm–3:00pm PT
- Thu, Feb 26 — 9:00am–10:00am PT

If none of those work, tell me what windows look like and we’ll adapt. I’ll bring Ben (SE) and request a calendar invite once you lock a slot.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0130

Attachment: pre-call-throughput-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Vanessa — thanks for the summary, that matches our notes. We can do Wed Feb 25 at 2pm PT (that works best for our infra lead).

Quick numbers to seed the template (I'll upload the spreadsheet later today):
- Peak sustained QPS (inference calls): 8
- Expected burst concurrency: 18–22 (10s–30s bursts during batch overlaps)
- Average tokens per request: ~420 tokens (prompt ~140 + context ~280)
- Target p95 latency: 200ms (we'd like P99 to be under 400ms but P95 is primary)

We'll attach our network diagram and a short runbook with the ticketing contact (DevOps). I'll also send the filled template before EOD so you have concrete numbers.

Ben — looping you in as the SE who will lead the throughput-run. Ben, brief agenda below; feel free to add any pre-read.

- 5m: intros + call objectives

Thanks — I’ll lead the SE portion Wednesday. Quick pre-call checklist attached and a short note on what I’ll be prepared to validate during the session:

Pre-call checklist (attached: dedicated-sizing-checklist.pdf)
- Filled throughput template (tokens, concurrency, percentiles)
- Sample payload example (anonymized) for performance profiling
- Network diagram and egress/NAT details
- Expected daily token volume and retention/trace requirements

What I’ll validate in the call
- Model family fit (quantized vs fp16 tradeoffs) and rough GPU footprint
- Batching/latency tradeoffs for your interactive path 
- KV cache expectations and warmup strategies for burst traffic
- Fallback model and regional routing policy recommendations

If you have the template uploaded any time today I’ll run a quick sizing sketch and share it ahead of the call so we can make the meeting action-oriented.

See you Wednesday —
Ben Carter
